assertion.interpretation: Zhou Yi's quoted refusal to flee, citing his position as a minister, is a prior statement that contextualizes his later conduct.
assertion.surface: 顗曰吾備位大臣朝廷傾撓豈可草間求活投身胡虜邪

valid_mentions.local_explanation: 郝嘏 is a person mentioned in the annotation as one who advised Zhou Yi to flee.
左右文武 refers collectively to the civil and military attendants/officials around Zhou Yi.
顗 is the personal name of Zhou Yi (周顗), mentioned in the annotation.
吾 is a first-person pronoun used by Zhou Yi to refer to himself.
王敦 is the full name of Wang Dun, mentioned in the 晉陽秋 annotation.
長史 is an office title (Chief Clerk) that here refers to Zhou Yi's position, but could also be a person reference to the person holding that office.
朝士 refers collectively to the court officials who went to see Wang Dun.
敦 is the personal name of Wang Dun, used in the annotation.
不對 implies a person responding (or not responding) to Wang Dun; the subject is implied but refers to a person.
力不足 is a phrase about insufficient strength, not a person reference.
位大臣 refers to a high-ranking minister, likely referring to Zhou Yi himself in the annotation context.
朝廷 refers to the imperial court as an institution, not a person.
胡虜 is a derogatory collective reference to non-Han peoples/enemies.
有餘 is a fragment about having surplus strength, not a person reference.
王大將軍 refers to Wang Dun (王敦), the General who rebelled. The title 大將軍 is used as an office title reference.
周伯仁 is the courtesy name of Zhou Yi (周顗), a person who went to see Wang Dun.
周 in 謂周曰 refers to 周伯仁 (Zhou Yi), addressed by his surname.
之 in 往見之 refers to 王大將軍 (Wang Dun), the person Zhou Boren went to see.
卿 is a second-person pronoun used by Wang Dun to address Zhou Boren.
公 in 以此負公 is an honorific used by Zhou Boren to address Wang Dun.
下官 is a self-deprecating reference used by Zhou Boren to refer to himself.
